candidate.title: Break-Seq
candidate.scope: The single Break-Seq route in the assigned Illumina schematic, from agarose-embedded chromosomal double-stranded DNA through end labeling, release/fragmentation, affinity capture, adapter attachment, and PCR/purification to a DNA library. The left replication-fork icon introduces breakage as biological context. The Hoffman et al. Break-seq full text clarifies this depiction; its Break-chip, RNA-seq, validation assays, and unshown experimental treatments are outside this extraction. Break-seq is a spelling variant of the card title, not a second workflow.

states.label: Chromosomal DNA containing breaks, trapped in agarose gel
features: Double-stranded chromosomal DNA is held in an agarose compartment before end labeling.
The central Break icon has offset strand discontinuities; the outer 5′/3′ labels show antiparallel strand orientation. The cartoon does not establish a uniform end structure for all substrates.
The biological target is chromosome double-strand breakage; replication-fork breakage is the illustrated context.

operations.label: End-repair with dGTP, dCTP, dTTP and biotinylated-dATP
operations.description: End-repair acts on the chromosomal DNA ends while the DNA remains in agarose, producing biotin-labeled end-associated DNA. The diagram supplies the nucleotide identities. The paper identifies T4 DNA polymerase in the End-It end-repair mix as the labeling component; the output represents labeled DNA ends, not a demonstrated ligation of the break.
operations.mechanism: The reported T4 DNA polymerase end-repair reaction incorporates the depicted biotinylated nucleotide. End-It is a component of this operation, not a separately targeted assay.
operations.information_effect: Introduces a physical affinity handle at end-repaired DNA regions before artificial fragmentation. End-proximal genomic DNA thereby becomes recoverable for break mapping.

operations.label: Elution and fragmentation
operations.description: Releases the labeled DNA from agarose and converts it into smaller duplex fragments; the output contains both label-bearing and unmarked fragments. This remains one combined operation at the level of the diagram. For the paper-associated Break-seq implementation, the main text identifies electroelution. The catalogue description instead says beta-agarase digestion, which the paper assigns to Break-chip; that catalogue detail is not substituted into the depicted elution block.
operations.mechanism: The diagram specifies elution and fragmentation without internal settings. The paper calls the fragmentation shearing and identifies electroelution for Break-seq.
operations.information_effect: Produces manageable genomic inserts while retaining the association between earlier end labeling and nearby sequence. The newly generated shearing ends do not all acquire the initial affinity label.

operations.description: Amplifies and purifies the adapter-bearing selected DNA, producing the final DNA library shown at the end of the schematic.

operations.information_effect: Preserves selected genomic inserts in a sequencing library. The paper reports aligning sequence reads to the yeast reference genome to identify regions of end-labeled signal. Sequencing and alignment explain the library readout here; they are not additional operations drawn in this schematic.

method_scopes.rationale: The card heading and the left diagram caption identify one target, Break-Seq/Break-seq. All five depicted processing instances belong to that route. The primary paper describes the same core sequence of in-gel DNA-end labeling, shearing, labeled-dsDNA capture, and multiplexed Illumina library construction. Break-chip appears in the paper and helps resolve the release-method discrepancy, but is not an alternative target in this image. End-It is a named reagent component. The input agarose state and the introductory fork icon do not require additional unshown processing branches.
